investigations.question: Does a server whose cached last log entry still exceeds its installed snapshot index decide vote requests differently from a server whose cached state matches its snapshot, and can a quorum of such servers be reached under permitted use?
investigations.hypothesis: requestVote and requestPreVote evaluate log completeness with getLastEntry, so a phantom claim replaces the installed snapshot as the voter's notion of its own log: the same request is granted by the phantom holder and rejected by a voter whose cached state is consistent. The phantom suffix was uncommitted (a quorum storing it would have committed it), so its holders were a minority of the configuration that created it, which bounds the effect to availability unless a configuration change later makes that group a majority.
investigations.discriminator: A five-voter history in which the deposed leader and one follower hold an uncommitted suffix while the other three commit a newer-term history and publish a snapshot below that suffix index; after both minority members install it, the same RequestVote (the stale follower's real log claim, carrying the leadership-transfer flag so the known-leader rejection does not mask the log test) is delivered to a phantom holder and to a consistent voter. A grant by the phantom holder together with a rejection by the consistent voter would establish the changed decision; an equal outcome would refute it.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index does not exceed its own cached last log index keeps advertising a log it no longer holds, fails every prev-log check from that leader and accepts no further log entry, while the leader retries the same snapshot indefinitely; the starvation ends only when a snapshot above the cached claim is published. Source basis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail, raft.go 1837-1977, tail at 1952-1977); getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); prev-log verification then misses below the log store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix (src_append_prev_check, raft.go 1458-1606); the leader walks nextIndex down one step per rejection (src_replicate_failure, replication.go 240-300) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, which jumps to SEND_SNAP and, on acceptance, resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result, replication.go 352-372); the non-monotonic compaction path keeps any suffix above the snapshot index while the monotonic branch (removeOldLogs, src_compaction) deletes the whole store without resetting the claim. Decided evidence, four receipts of the same experiment family: the trimmed case reproduces the signature in every run (settled comparison set in execution b6089b103bbb467199d051f4492e82c8: repeated_snapshot_installs, victim_not_caught_up and stale_claim_persists all hold on the trimmed probe at index 14, with the untrimmed control negative on the same fields at index 29), and the fourth receipt resolves both boundaries. Monotonic store (execution 20c7c72772474093bd6093a37b84448f, probe at index 14): restores 5 -> 1102 in the 3s window with applied index fixed at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95, the cached claim persisting, and the log store emptied to first index 0 / last index 0 - so the stall does not depend on a surviving suffix, only on the cached claim outranking the installed snapshot. Repair boundary (same receipt, probe at index 33): the stall was measured before the intervention, then the leader's applied index was driven past the follower's claim of 97, a snapshot at 98 was published, and the follower resumed - applied 83 -> 109 equal to the frontier, commit index 109, cached claim repaired to a consistent value - which confirms the stated bound: the starvation lasts while the newest snapshot stays at or below the claim and ends when one lands above it. A successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower never campaigned: every receipt shows one stable leader set for the whole window with the follower's term fixed, so the starved state is stable rather than self-healing by election.

history.question: When a leader must ship a snapshot to a follower whose own log already extends beyond the leader's snapshot index (stale suffix, lower term), does the follower accept subsequent log entries, and does its advertised log state stay consistent with the log it actually holds?
history.hypothesis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied/lastSnapshot/config but never resets the cached last log entry, and compactLogs leaves the follower's stale suffix on disk (non-monotonic store) or deletes everything below it (monotonic store). Because getLastEntry prefers lastLogIndex when it is >= lastSnapshotIndex, the follower keeps advertising a log it no longer has, fails every prev-log check, and the leader can only retry the same snapshot (SEND_SNAP) forever: no entry is ever accepted after the install.
history.discriminator: Retained receipt of the focused probe: repeated InstallSnapshot acceptance (FSM Restore count rising while the leader's snapshot index is unchanged), the follower's applied index staying at the leader's snapshot index while the cluster frontier advances, and the follower's cached last-log index/term remaining beyond the installed snapshot index; the untrimmed control separates the snapshot-install trigger from the mere existence of a stale suffix.

investigations.question: Does a server whose cached last log entry still exceeds its installed snapshot index decide vote requests differently from a server whose cached state matches its snapshot, and can a quorum of such servers be reached under permitted use?
investigations.hypothesis: requestVote and requestPreVote evaluate log completeness with getLastEntry, so a phantom claim replaces the installed snapshot as the voter's notion of its own log: the same request is granted by the phantom holder and rejected by a voter whose cached state is consistent. The phantom suffix was uncommitted (a quorum storing it would have committed it), so its holders were a minority of the configuration that created it, which bounds the effect to availability unless a configuration change later makes that group a majority.
investigations.discriminator: A five-voter history in which the deposed leader and one follower hold an uncommitted suffix while the other three commit a newer-term history and publish a snapshot below that suffix index; after both minority members install it, the same RequestVote (the stale follower's real log claim, carrying the leadership-transfer flag so the known-leader rejection does not mask the log test) is delivered to a phantom holder and to a consistent voter. A grant by the phantom holder together with a rejection by the consistent voter would establish the changed decision; an equal outcome would refute it.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: in this revision, a follower that accepts a snapshot while its own cached log extends at or beyond the leader's snapshot index is left with an inconsistent log claim and never accepts another log entry from that leader. Basis: installSnapshot updates lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (raft.go 1930-1977), while getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (state.go 160-175). Compaction cannot remove the stale suffix in the non-monotonic store path when TrailingLogs exceeds the log length (snapshot.go 217-252), so the follower's store keeps entries above the snapshot index whose terms differ from the leader's; every AppendEntries prev-log check then either misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix, the leader's nextIndex is only decremented one step per rejection (replication.go 247-252) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, and the leader responds by re-shipping the same snapshot (replication.go 296-300, 352-372). Restricted to the measured conditions: three voters, in-memory store, FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10, an idle cluster plus steady new writes, and a follower restarted on its real on-disk log whose orphan suffix (indexes beyond the leader's snapshot index, lower term) is preserved. Local construction feedback for the same harness (native feedback only, not a retained receipt) showed the follower's FSM restored 4 -> 1365 times in a 3s window while the leader's snapshot index stayed at 83, the follower's applied index stayed at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95, the follower's cached last log claim stayed (98, term 2) against snapshot (83, term 3), its commit index stayed 0, and its store kept indexes 84-98; the untrimmed control on the identical history accepted no snapshot, repaired the suffix with entries and caught up (applied 83 -> 95). Counterevidence considered: the concern that the follower's own election timeout would repair the situation is not observed, because a successful InstallSnapshot refreshes lastContact, so no spurious election fires; and the control refutes 'any stale suffix stalls replication'. Limits: the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained run of the requested experiment; the reachability of the trigger in production depends on a voter whose log suffix is both longer than the leader's snapshot index and stale in term (a deposed leader or a follower that stored entries from a superseded leader) together with log trimming on the leader; monotonic-store deployments delete the stale suffix instead of keeping it, so their failure mode (entry starvation with the leader's snapshot index at or below the cached claim) still needs its own receipt.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control with the same history repaired the stale suffix using log entries alone, so a stale suffix by itself is not sufficient; the install-snapshot path with a trimmed leader log is the trigger.
The successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower does not force an election and the starved state is stable rather than transient in the measured configuration.
limitations: The measured configuration used in-memory stores plus a file snapshot store, TrailingLogs=10, three voters, and a restarted ex-leader that kept an orphan suffix; other TrailingLogs, monotonic stores and larger clusters are not measured here.
Probe fields are read from the follower's cached state and its log store on the same process; the receipt is needed before treating the numbers as retained observations.

Basis, retained receipt (execution d1897256143f4de2b0477a3460ae392b, exit 0, both generated cases passed): in the trimmed case the setup event (index 0) recorded the victim's cached last log claim (index 95, term 2) with the leader's snapshot at index 83/term 3, its store 1-95 intact and zero restores; after reconnecting, the probe event (index 14) recorded the victim's FSM restored 4 -> 1193 times inside the 3s window with the leader's snapshot index still 83 (leader_snapshot_is_unchanged true), the victim's applied index unchanged at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95 with new entries committed and applied elsewhere, the cached claim still (index 95, term 2) with the store suffix 84-95 kept, the victim's commit index still 0, and exactly one stable leader set over the window. The untrimmed control on the same history (setup index 15, probe index 29) accepted no snapshot at all (restores 0, repeated_snapshot_installs false), repaired the claim with entries (index 95, term 3) and caught up (applied 83 -> 95, commit 95), which excludes the mere existence of the stale suffix as the cause. The five declared comparisons resolved unknown, not holds: the admission event ca_setup carried no tag field, so the trimmed_setup/untrimmed_setup alias conditions could not be evaluated and the admission could not be associated ('Missing operation admission fields or identity', 'Ambiguous prerequisite association; missing trimmed_setup.tag'); the successor experiment fixes exactly that field. The raw retained values therefore support the account, but the comparison-level verdict, and with it the formal conclusion, is still pending. Limits: three voters, in-memory log store with a file snapshot store, TrailingLogs=10, a restarted ex-leader whose orphan suffix came from applies it accepted while partitioned, a 3s idle-plus-steady-writes window, and a single induced full partition; the vote-side consequence of the stale claim (knowledge-1) never triggered because no election occurred, the monotonic-store variant deletes the suffix instead of keeping it and needs its own receipt, and nothing here measures whether the state persists beyond the window or whether a larger cluster with several trimmed voters could still repair the node.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control accepted no snapshot, repaired the stale suffix with ordinary log entries and reached the cluster frontier, so a stale log suffix by itself does not stall replication; the trimmed leader log plus the install path is the trigger.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index does not exceed its own cached last log index keeps advertising a log it no longer holds, fails every prev-log check from that leader and accepts no further log entry, while the leader retries the same snapshot indefinitely; the starvation ends only when a snapshot above the cached claim is published. Source basis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail, raft.go 1837-1977, tail at 1952-1977); getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); prev-log verification then misses below the log store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix (src_append_prev_check, raft.go 1458-1606); the leader walks nextIndex down one step per rejection (src_replicate_failure, replication.go 240-300) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, which jumps to SEND_SNAP and, on acceptance, resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result, replication.go 352-372); the non-monotonic compaction path keeps any suffix above the snapshot index while the monotonic branch (removeOldLogs, src_compaction) deletes the whole store without resetting the claim. Decided evidence, four receipts of the same experiment family: the trimmed case reproduces the signature in every run (settled comparison set in execution b6089b103bbb467199d051f4492e82c8: repeated_snapshot_installs, victim_not_caught_up and stale_claim_persists all hold on the trimmed probe at index 14, with the untrimmed control negative on the same fields at index 29), and the fourth receipt resolves both boundaries. Monotonic store (execution 20c7c72772474093bd6093a37b84448f, probe at index 14): restores 5 -> 1102 in the 3s window with applied index fixed at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95, the cached claim persisting, and the log store emptied to first index 0 / last index 0 - so the stall does not depend on a surviving suffix, only on the cached claim outranking the installed snapshot. Repair boundary (same receipt, probe at index 33): the stall was measured before the intervention, then the leader's applied index was driven past the follower's claim of 97, a snapshot at 98 was published, and the follower resumed - applied 83 -> 109 equal to the frontier, commit index 109, cached claim repaired to a consistent value - which confirms the stated bound: the starvation lasts while the newest snapshot stays at or below the claim and ends when one lands above it. Safety-relevant reading of the same root cause: the phantom claim is also what requestVote uses for its own log (src_vote_log_check), so the voter's notion of its log can outrank its durable snapshot. Reasoning bounds this: the phantom suffix lies beyond the commit index of the term that created it, so its holders were a minority of that configuration, and a leader's snapshot index can never fall below committed history; a quorum of phantoms therefore needs a configuration change that turns that minority into a majority of a new configuration, which is not measured and is the discriminator of the child question registered with this update. Limits: measured configuration is three voters, InmemStore plus FileSnapshotStore (and its monotonic wrapper), TrailingLogs=10 against a large control, an idle cluster with one write per 250ms sample, 3-4s windows and one induced partition; the follower's commit index stays 0 through the install path and is reported as an advertised-state inconsistency rather than an independent defect; production BoltDB-style stores, other TrailingLogs values, longer windows, larger clusters and the vote-decision consequence remain subject to their own receipts.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control accepted no snapshot, repaired the stale suffix with ordinary log entries and reached the cluster frontier in every run, so a stale suffix alone does not stall replication; the trimmed leader log together with the install path is the trigger.

A successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower never campaigned: every receipt shows one stable leader set for the whole window with the follower's term fixed, so the starved state is stable rather than self-healing by election.

The starvation is bounded, not permanent: the repair probe shows recovery once a snapshot above the cached claim is published (claim 97, snapshot 98, follower then applied to the frontier), so the claim is that starvation lasts while the newest snapshot index stays at or below the claim.

The monotonic-store case empties the log store and still stalls, so the surviving on-disk suffix is not required for the defect; this narrows the cause to the cached log claim and the snapshot index relationship.
limitations: Measured configuration only: three voters, InmemStore plus FileSnapshotStore (and its in-process monotonic wrapper), TrailingLogs=10 against a large control, an idle cluster with one write per 250ms sample, 3-4s windows and a single induced partition.
